correctness.rationale: Maximal graphic-arrangement chambers correspond to acyclic wheel orientations; smoothness is characterized integrally by spanning-tree Hasse graphs. Acyclic mixed-spoke orientations have forced crossing arcs and independent run orientations; an exact cover-edge count shows smoothness iff each S-run has one sink and T-run one source. Weighted cyclic compositions yield the binomial spectrum and logarithmic generating function. Uniform-spoke cases each give 2m. The wheel chromatic polynomial gives 3^m-3 total. A distinct standalone exhaustive DAG checker verifies the all-k formula for m=3..9 (VERIFY_OK). Finite computation is explicitly not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The wheel is the smallest natural family combining a hub and a cyclic rim, moving from a complete graph (all fixed points smooth at m=3) to genuinely non-simple graphic zonotopes. The exact number of smooth torus-fixed points, full incoming-spoke stratification, and exponential decay of the smooth fraction quantify local regularity across an infinite characteristic-independent toric family. Ordinary face enumeration and global simplicity classification alone do not provide the precise invariant. The statement does not claim the full singular locus or nonfixed orbits.
